summary: Turns the search page into a client component. It reads q from the URL, fetches matching products and lists them under a heading that shows the query.

findings.title: Reflected XSS through the search query heading
findings.description: The heading injects the raw q URL parameter as HTML through dangerouslySetInnerHTML. No code escapes or sanitizes the query first. An attacker can send a victim a link whose q value carries script. That script then runs in the victim's session on this origin. Render the query as a normal text child so React escapes it.
findings.problem: The heading injects the raw q URL parameter as HTML through dangerouslySetInnerHTML. No code escapes or sanitizes the query first.
findings.consequence: An attacker can send a victim a link whose q value carries script. That script then runs in the victim's session on this origin.
findings.fix: Render the query as a normal text child so React escapes it.

findings.title: Effect without dependencies refetches on every render
findings.description: The effect has no dependency array, so it runs after every render. Each response calls setResults with a new array, which renders again and starts another fetch. The page sends search requests to the catalog API in an endless loop. This loads the backend and drains the user's network and battery. Give the effect a dependency array containing query.

findings.consequence: The page sends search requests to the catalog API in an endless loop. This loads the backend and drains the user's network and battery.
findings.fix: Give the effect a dependency array containing query.

findings.title: Hooks called after a conditional early return
findings.description: SearchPage returns early when q is empty, before it calls useState and useEffect. So the number of hooks the component calls changes between renders. If the user navigates on the client from no query to a query, React throws because the hook count changed. The search page then crashes. Call useState and useEffect before the early return. Inside the effect, skip the fetch when query is empty.

findings.consequence: If the user navigates on the client from no query to a query, React throws because the hook count changed. The search page then crashes.
findings.fix: Call useState and useEffect before the early return. Inside the effect, skip the fetch when query is empty.

findings.title: Search failure leaves an unhandled rejection
findings.description: searchProducts throws when the response is not ok. The effect chains only then on the promise and never handles the rejection. A failed search produces an unhandled rejection. The user sees an empty list with no error message. Add a catch handler that records the error in state and shows it to the user.
